evidence.quote: Today the Federal Open Market Committee reaffirmed the current 0 to ¼ percent target range for the federal funds rate.
economic conditions are currently anticipated to evolve in a manner that will warrant only gradual increases in the target federal funds rate.
It’s not an ironclad guarantee, but we anticipate that that’s something that will be appropriate later this year.
Inflation has continued to run below our longer-run objective, in part reflecting lower energy prices.
So, although progress clearly has been achieved, room for further improvement remains.
On the one hand, waiting too long to begin normalization can risk significantly overshooting our inflation objective given the lags in the operation of monetary policy.

parsed.rationale: The Chair holds rates at zero and signals a likely first hike later this year, but stresses gradual increases, a lowered dot path, below-target inflation and remaining slack. Risks are presented as two-sided, so the net signal is roughly balanced with a slight dovish tilt.
